In particular, is the FR-8 '2%' tolerance (relative vs percentage points, and against which baseline) unambiguous given that Section 10.3 says 'default 2' with no unit?","rationale":"FR-8 governs the cost-versus-approval trade-off, and its acceptance test relies on one clear reading of the tolerance.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["1","2.1","2.2","3","10.3","24"]},{"id":"RQ-002","criterion_id":"fitness_for_objectives","question":"Does the Redis fast path keyed idem:resp:{idempotency_key} (without merchant_id and without checking the request hash) satisfy P3 and FR-5, given that merchants are allowed to use order or invoice IDs as keys?","rationale":"Keys from different merchants could collide, which would return one merchant's stored response to another and skip the 422 check on a reused body.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["3","9.1","9.2","2.1"]},{"id":"RQ-003","criterion_id":"claims_and_external_constraints","question":"Is Section 9.3's claim correct that a single DynamoDB partition sustains 10,000 WCU/s? Can a merchant_id partition key with an LSI carry about 1,800 WCU at peak for one merchant, given the per-partition limit, the 10 GB LSI item-collection limit and the fact that an LSI blocks partition splitting?","rationale":"The capacity argument for the confirmed idempotency store, and its 'Ready' status, rests on this per-partition figure.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["DynamoDB per partition write capacity limit 1000 WCU","DynamoDB local secondary index item collection size limit 10 GB","DynamoDB split for heat local secondary index"],"section_refs":["9.3","24","27"]},{"id":"RQ-004","criterion_id":"claims_and_external_constraints","question":"Do PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 really allow a merchant or service provider to keep the CVC in encrypted form after authorization, until settlement or for 72 hours, for cascades and incremental authorizations? Or does Requirement 3.3.1 forbid storing SAD after authorization, with 3.3.2 covering only pre-authorization storage and 3.3.3 covering issuers?","rationale":"NFR-6 and the confirmed CVC-handling decision rest on this reading, and if it is wrong it puts the Level 1 assessment in NFR-5 at risk.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["PCI DSS v4.0 requirement 3.3.1 sensitive authentication data not retained after authorization","PCI DSS v4.0 requirement 3.3.2 SAD stored electronically prior to completion of authorization","PCI DSS v4.0.1 retirement of v4.0"],"section_refs":["12.4","2.2","24"]},{"id":"RQ-005","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"Does the Fraud Hook's detokenisation of the PAN (under the Card Adapter's service role) and its sending of the PAN to FRV-1 contradict P2, the CDE scope table in 12.2 (Fraud Hook 'Out of scope'), and the rule that only the Card Adapter may call detokenise?","rationale":"If the PAN reaches the Fraud Hook, the CDE boundary that NFR-5 relies on is wrong and the segmentation claim fails.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["3","12.1","12.2","13.1","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-006","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"Does a payout bank-account change protect against account takeover when TOTP is optional for Finance users, no step-up or out-of-band confirmation is required, and the confirmation email goes only to the user who made the change?","rationale":"FR-13 and FR-17 send merchant money to whatever account is registered, so a takeover of a Finance account would let funds be redirected.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["18.2","18.3","18.4","24"]},{"id":"RQ-007","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"Does running all primary data stores in Singapore, with DR in Jakarta, meet the data-localisation and cross-border transfer obligations for payment data in the markets served (especially Indonesia under Bank Indonesia payment-system rules and Law 27/2022)? Does sending personal data to FRV-1 without a signed DPA conflict with NFR-7?","rationale":"NFR-7 requires lawful processing in every market, and a localisation mandate could prevent operation in that market.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["Bank Indonesia regulation payment transaction data processing domestic localisation","Indonesia Law 27 2022 cross-border personal data transfer requirements","Thailand PDPA cross-border transfer adequacy requirements"],"section_refs":["2.2","19.1","13.1","25"]},{"id":"RQ-008","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"Can NFR-4 (RPO zero on loss of a region) hold when Aurora Global Database replication is asynchronous (20.2)? Can the NFR-4 acceptance test, which requires every posting committed before the failure to be present after failover, pass?","rationale":"A zero-RPO requirement that contradicts the confirmed DR design means ledger data can be lost or the requirement can never be signed off.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["Aurora Global Database replication lag RPO unplanned failover","Aurora Global Database managed failover data loss"],"section_refs":["2.2","20.2","24","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-009","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"Does Section 21.1's claim that 'fewer than 1% of card payments cascade' match the 3.8% retryable rate in 10.5 and the 3.8% injection in the NFR-2 test? Given the 2,500 ms attempt timeout, can the p99 of 1,500 ms in NFR-2 be met once cascades fall inside the 99th percentile?","rationale":"If cascades sit inside the p99, NFR-2 cannot be met as designed and the latency budget is unsupported.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["10.5","11.1","21.1","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-010","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"Are the build phase statuses consistent with the requirements and decisions? Specifically: the Fraud Hook (Phase 8) comes after the first go-live (after Phase 7) although FR-9 is mandatory; network tokens are confirmed 'from launch' and Phase 3 is 'No - ready' although the TRID application has not been submitted (Backlog 2); and the Vault is marked 'Ready'.","rationale":"The first cohort could go live without FR-9 fraud scoring or FR-14 network tokens, against the confirmed decisions.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["2.1","24","25","27","28"]},{"id":"RQ-011","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"When an attempt times out after 2,500 ms and the transaction cascades to another acquirer, what stops a double authorization if the first acquirer approves late? Late responses are 'discarded', and the document describes no reversal or void.","rationale":"Section 11.2's claim that cascading 'cannot create a duplicate charge' and the FR-5 promise of at most one authorization both depend on this.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["11.1","11.2","20.3"]},{"id":"RQ-012","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"Is a single CloudHSM in one AZ (with scale-out triggered at 1,500 card TPS, which the design's 55% card share of 2,000 TPS never reaches) compatible with NFR-3 at 99.95% and with the throughput needed for detokenise and tokenise at about 1,100 card TPS plus cascades? Also, does a Vault 503 mapped to 'retryable' just cascade into the same failure?","rationale":"The HSM is a single point of failure for every card payment, so it directly affects NFR-1 and NFR-3.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["AWS CloudHSM single HSM availability recommendation multiple AZ","AWS CloudHSM operations per second AES unwrap performance hsm2m.medium"],"section_refs":["12.3","20.1","21.1","24","2.2"]},{"id":"RQ-013","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"Can NFR-8 (reports by 08:00 SGT on T+1) be met at 2027 volume? The matcher waits for every file, the latest arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT), and the measured run is 45 + 15 minutes at 2025 volume, about half the target volume. What happens when a file is late or missing?","rationale":"NFR-8 is a merchant-facing SLA, and the arithmetic from the document's own figures appears to exceed it.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["16.1","16.2","2.2","26.2"]},{"id":"RQ-014","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"After a regional failover, DynamoDB and Redis start empty and idempotency state is 'reconstructed from the payment table', but that table has no idempotency_key or request_hash. Is FR-5 kept across failover? Does the sweeper handle IN_PROGRESS locks for requests that crashed before a payment existed?","rationale":"Duplicate authorizations during retry storms after failover would break FR-5 and P7.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["9.2","19","20.2","20.3"]},{"id":"RQ-015","criterion_id":"assumptions_and_dependencies","question":"Which unverified premises does the design depend on: TRID/network-token certification timing, the FRV-1 contract and SLA, sample files from ACQ-PH1 and WAG-1, scheme approval of cross-acquirer cascading on soft decline 05, and the cascade recovery rate taken from a single pilot? Is each tracked to closure with an owner and a date?","rationale":"Confirmed decisions and 'Ready' ratings rest on pending items, and these can delay launch or invalidate FR-7 and FR-14.","needs_external":true,"capability":"none","queries":["Visa reattempt rules decline categories excessive reattempts","Mastercard merchant advice code transaction retry rules","Visa Token Service token requestor onboarding timeline"],"section_refs":["11.1","11.3","12.5","25","27"]},{"id":"RQ-016","criterion_id":"verifiability","question":"Can each acceptance criterion in Section 26 verify its requirement? In particular: FR-5 tests only sequential replay, not concurrency; FR-8 tests the acquirer chosen, not the change in authorization rate; NFR-4 has no RPO measurement method; NFR-9 does not cover the 45%-share merchant; NFR-6 assumes the CVC storage is permitted.","rationale":"Section 26 is the basis of the Phase 9 test plan, so weak criteria let unmet requirements pass.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["26.1","26.2","2.1","2.2"]},{"id":"RQ-017","criterion_id":"verifiability","question":"Which performance claims need a benchmark before build: the latency budget built by summing component p99s, the 20 ms HSM unwrap 'vendor benchmark', the Aurora 2,600 TPS spike, and the MSK throughput on three m7g.xlarge brokers?","rationale":"NFR-1 and NFR-2 sign-off depends on these figures, and some of them come only from vendor numbers or short spikes.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["21.1","21.2","12.3"]},{"id":"RQ-018","criterion_id":"requirement_completeness","question":"Are any controls or paths missing? Candidates: authorization reversal on cascade or timeout; a residue account for fee rounding, which is not in the chart of accounts; handling of late or missing settlement files; reconciliation of the asynchronous notifications for wallets and bank transfers; and a precise expiry-sweeper policy per scheme.","rationale":"FR-7, FR-10 and FR-11 need these paths to be complete for the ledger and reconciliation to stay correct.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["7.2","11.2","14.1","15","16.2"]},{"id":"RQ-019","criterion_id":"decision_preservation","question":"Which confirmed decisions might the evidence challenge, and does each challenge meet the bar of two or more evidence items? The candidates are CVC handling, one HSM at launch, idempotency store keying, DR with zero RPO, network tokens from launch, and the cascade policy on 05. Can the proposed refinements preserve or refine these decisions instead?","rationale":"Approved decisions may be challenged only with strong evidence, so the review must be explicit about which ones it challenges.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["24","12.3","12.4","9.2","20.2"]},{"id":"RQ-020","criterion_id":"operability_and_governance","question":"Are owners named for the weekly Routing Review, the Finance Ops exception queue, the on-call for payout freezes and projection discrepancies, the HSM scale-out trigger, and the go-live risk acceptance for gaps such as fraud and disputes? Are cost and monitoring (projection lag, sweeper escalations) given SLOs?","rationale":"Several controls depend on human processes, and without accountable owners there is no assurance those controls run.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["10.3","14.3","16.2","20.3","22","27","28"]},{"id":"RQ-021","criterion_id":"fitness_for_objectives","question":"Are the webhook SSRF controls, the signing and retry schedule, the transactional outbox with the ledger in the same transaction, and integer minor-unit money handling fit for FR-10, FR-12 and P4/P5/P7, so that they can be affirmed as strengths?","rationale":"The review should affirm design elements that are fit for purpose and not only list defects.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["7.2","14.3","15","17"]}],"criteria_skipped":[]}

{"intent_summary":{"statement":"MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform. It accepts merchant payment requests, routes each one to an acquirer, e-wallet provider or bank-transfer rail, and accounts for every resulting movement of money until it is settled to the merchant. It replaces five per-market integration stacks with one merchant API across five Southeast Asian markets. Scope covers acceptance, routing, retries, idempotency, vaulting, fraud-scoring integration, a double-entry ledger, reconciliation, payouts, webhooks and a merchant admin plane, for about 15,000 merchants at a peak of 2,000 TPS. Disputes case management, KYB, 3DS server internals, lending/BNPL and checkout UIs are out of scope.","objectives":[{"ref":null,"text":"Replace five per-market integration stacks (no shared routing or ledger, spreadsheet reconciliation) with one platform and one versioned merchant API across SG, MY, ID, TH and PH."},{"ref":null,"text":"Serve approximately 15,000 active merchants and a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS by the 2027 design target."},{"ref":"P1","text":"One payment, one truth: the payment record and the ledger are the source of truth; provider responses are only inputs."},{"ref":"P2","text":"Card data stays in the Vault; PAN and SAD leave the Vault boundary only over the Card Adapter's connection to an acquirer; all other services handle tokens only."},{"ref":"P3","text":"Idempotency is scoped to the (merchant, key) pair for every mutating call."},{"ref":"P4","text":"Money is integers: integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code; no floating-point amounts."},{"ref":"P5","text":"The ledger is append-only; corrections are new reversing or adjusting journals."},{"ref":"P6","text":"Adapters absorb provider differences; the core never branches on provider identity."},{"ref":"P7","text":"At-least-once delivery with exactly-once effect via consumer deduplication on stable identifiers."},{"ref":"P8","text":"Fail closed on security; degrade gracefully to documented defaults on optional enrichment (fraud signals, BIN metadata)."},{"ref":"P9","text":"Least privilege and separation of duties; money-moving permissions are separate from configuration permissions."},{"ref":"P10","text":"Everything is auditable: every mutation, routing decision and admin action can be reconstructed."},{"ref":"NFR-2","text":"Card authorization p99 at most 1,500 ms end to end, including cascade; orchestration overhead p99 at most 250 ms."},{"ref":"NFR-3","text":"Merchant payment API monthly availability of at least 99.95%."},{"ref":"NFR-4","text":"RPO zero for authorized payments and ledger postings, including on loss of an AWS region; RTO 30 minutes."},{"ref":"FR-8","text":"Prefer the lowest-cost eligible acquirer unless this lowers the expected authorization rate by more than 2%."}],"constraints":[{"ref":"NFR-5","text":"Assessment as a PCI DSS v4.0 Level 1 service provider, with the CDE limited to the components listed in Section 12.2."},{"ref":"NFR-6","text":"SAD handled per PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3.2.1 and 3.3.2: stored only encrypted in the Vault and deleted at settlement."},{"ref":"NFR-7","text":"Personal data processed under SG PDPA 2012, MY PDPA 2010, ID Law 27/2022, TH PDPA 2019 and PH DPA 2012, including purpose limitation, retention limits and access logging."},{"ref":"FR-7","text":"Card scheme reattempt rules: never reattempt where the scheme prohibits it."},{"ref":null,"text":"Primary hosting on AWS ap-southeast-1 across three AZs; DR secondary in ap-southeast-3."},{"ref":null,"text":"The foundational principles take precedence over any later section that conflicts with them."},{"ref":null,"text":"Out of scope: KYB/onboarding (Merchant Risk platform supplies an approved-merchant event), 3DS server internals, dispute case management, and lending/BNPL."},{"ref":null,"text":"ACQ-PH1 retires API v2 in Q3 2027, so the adapter must migrate to v3 before then."},{"ref":"NFR-12","text":"Audit records are immutable and retained for five years; payment and attempt records are kept 7 years."}],"key_assumptions":[{"ref":null,"text":"2027 volume targets: 10.5 M attempts/day, 2,000 peak TPS, card share 55%, and the largest merchant at 45% of peak (about 900 TPS)."},{"ref":null,"text":"Fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, so the cascade path sits above p99 (2025 baseline: 3.8% retryable outcomes, about 31% recovered in the pilot)."},{"ref":null,"text":"PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3.2.1/3.3.2 permit storing encrypted CVC until settlement, and acquirers need the CVC for cascade re-presentation and incremental authorizations."},{"ref":null,"text":"FRV-1 needs the full PAN for its consortium velocity graph; the Fraud Hook obtains it through Vault detokenise."},{"ref":null,"text":"One CloudHSM with daily backups is enough until sustained card volume exceeds 1,500 TPS."},{"ref":null,"text":"Network tokens are available from launch, although token-requestor onboarding has not been submitted (Backlog item 2)."},{"ref":null,"text":"Settlement files arrive daily at stated local times, and the matcher (45 min at 2025 volume) plus reports (15 min) finish by 08:00 SGT."},{"ref":null,"text":"Aurora sizing is based on a spike test of 2,600 TPS on db.r7g.8xlarge; latency budget components come from load tests, vendor benchmarks and 2025 production p99."},{"ref":null,"text":"The first cohort (Singapore, cards and PayNow) can go live after Phase 7, with Finance Operations handling disputes manually and merchants using the portal."}],"doc_anchors":[{"doc_id":"DOC-design_v1","section_ref":"1","requirement_ids":[],"quote":"MPOP replaces five per-market integration stacks that share no routing, no ledger, and reconcile by spreadsheet.","page":1},{"doc_id":"DOC-design_v1","section_ref":"1","requirement_ids":[],"quote":"Payment acceptance, routing, retries, idempotency, vaulting, fraud-scoring integration, ledger, reconciliation, merchant","page":2},{"doc_id":"DOC-design_v1","section_ref":"1","requirement_ids":[],"quote":"MPOP provides one merchant API across five markets; As written, the Fraud Hook, its network path and a third-party vendor all come into PCI scope. NFR-5's limited CDE cannot be achieved, and a shared service identity defeats P9 least privilege.

recommendation.issue: The fast-path cache key is not scoped to the merchant and does not bind the request hash.

recommendation.verification: Extend the FR-5 test: two merchants send the same key and each gets its own payment, and a body-mismatch test returns 422 when the response is served from the Redis fast path.

findings.statement: The fast path stores and looks up responses at idem:resp:{idempotency_key}, with no merchant scope and no request-hash comparison. Section 9.1 says merchants often use their own order IDs as keys, so two merchants can easily share a key. In that case one merchant receives another merchant's stored payment response, which leaks data and suppresses a real payment. A reused key with a different body also gets the cached response instead of HTTP 422. This breaks P3 and the FR-5 contract.
findings.title: Redis idempotency fast path is keyed only on the key and skips the body-hash check

findings.statement: NFR-4 requires zero RPO for authorised payments and ledger postings even when the whole region is lost. Section 20.2 relies on Aurora Global Database replication, which the document itself calls asynchronous with typical lag under one second. On an unplanned regional loss, recently committed postings can be lost, so the NFR-4 game-day criterion cannot be passed reliably. Either the requirement or the approved DR decision has to change.
findings.title: Zero RPO on region loss conflicts with asynchronous Aurora Global replication

Lower the per-attempt timeout or make it budget-derived, and replace the under-1% claim with a modelled p99 at 3.8% retryable. Alternatively, restate NFR-2 so it excludes timeout cascades, with the owner's agreement.

recommendation.rationale: NFR-2 explicitly includes cascades, and the design's own data contradicts the under-1% premise.
recommendation.verification: Run the NFR-2 benchmark with a 3.8% retryable mix that includes timeouts, and report p99 separately for cascaded and non-cascaded paths.

findings.statement: Section 21.1 excludes cascades from p99 on the grounds that fewer than 1% of card payments cascade. The design's own baseline puts retryable outcomes at 3.8%, and the NFR-2 test injects 3.8%. So cascade paths fall inside the 99th percentile. A timeout-triggered cascade alone waits 2,500 ms before the second attempt, which already exceeds the 1,500 ms NFR-2 limit, and NFR-2 explicitly covers 'including any cascade'. NFR-2 is therefore not achievable as designed.
findings.title: Latency budget assumes under 1% of payments cascade, but the baseline retryable rate is 3.8%
